slot.brief: Express a physical quantity (e.g., from an unfamiliar named formula) in base units and identify its dimensional formula

stem: The dimensionless Ohnesorge number is $Oh=\dfrac{\eta}{\sqrt{\rho\sigma d}}$, where $\eta$ is dynamic viscosity, $\rho$ is density, and $d$ is a length. What is the dimensional formula of $\sigma$?
working:
$[Oh]=1 \Rightarrow [\sigma]=\dfrac{[\eta]^2}{[\rho][d]}$.
$[\eta]=[M L^{-1}T^{-1}],\quad [\rho]=[M L^{-3}],\quad [d]=[L]$.
$[\sigma]=\dfrac{[M^2L^{-2}T^{-2}]}{[M L^{-2}]}=[M L^0T^{-2}]$.
SI base units: $\text{kg s}^{-2}$.

Independent check: Since $[\eta]=[M L^{-1}T^{-1}]$ and $[\rho d]=[M L^{-2}]$, $[\sigma]=[\eta]^2/([\rho][d])=[M T^{-2}]$.
solution:
Since $Oh$ is dimensionless, $[\text{σ}]=[η]^2/([ρ][d])$.
$$[\text{σ}]=\frac{[M L^{-1}T^{-1}]^2}{[M L^{-3}][L]}=[M L^0T^{-2}]$$
